questions.text: Why does Kamila paraphrase lectures in her journal?
questions.hint: "If I can say what someone said in my own words, I actually know it."

questions.text: Professor Aidarov said language change was a form of decay.
questions.hint: "He told the students that this is not decay but adaptation."

questions.text: What did Aidarov say about Kazakh absorbing Russian words?
opts: It was a sign of weakness
It was a sign of contact between peoples
It was caused by Russian imperialism
questions.correct: It was a sign of contact between peoples
questions.hint: "He said this was not a sign of weakness but of contact — and that contact between languages is usually a sign of contact between peoples."

questions.text: Aidarov told students to read ___ .
questions.hint: "He told us to read Aitmatov."

questions.text: What did Amir add about endangered languages?
opts: Small languages are always the most endangered
Large languages can disappear if bilingual speakers stop transmitting them
Only government policy can save them
questions.correct: Large languages can disappear if bilingual speakers stop transmitting them
questions.hint: "The most endangered languages in the world were not necessarily the smallest..."

questions.text: Kamila concludes reported speech is really about:
opts: Paying attention to what people actually say
questions.correct: Paying attention to what people actually say
questions.hint: "reported speech... was a way of paying attention to what people actually said."

questions.text: What did Rustam ask Professor Aidarov?
opts: About language purism in a globalised world
questions.correct: About language purism in a globalised world
questions.hint: "I asked him whether he thought language purism was possible in a globalised world."

questions.text: What did Aidarov say about purism?
opts: Probably impossible, but the impulse is understandable
questions.correct: Probably impossible, but the impulse is understandable
questions.hint: "He said it probably wasn't, but that the impulse behind it was understandable."

questions.text: Aidarov said the research project was about language contact in ___ Kazakhstan.
questions.hint: "a project on language contact in western Kazakhstan"

questions.text: What did Aidarov say the selection criteria were?
questions.hint: "they were looking for students with curiosity and commitment — not necessarily those with the highest grades."

questions.text: Aidarov told Rustam to email ___ in the research office.
questions.hint: "He told me to email Dr Serikova in the research office."

questions.text: Zhibek decided not to apply for the research position.
questions.hint: "I'm going to apply. I love the idea of research on Kazakh language contact."

questions.text: "I study linguistics." → She said ___.
questions.hint: Backshift: Present Simple → Past Simple. "She said she STUDIED linguistics." ✅

questions.text: "I'll call you." → She said she ___ call.
questions.hint: Backshift: will → would. "She said she WOULD call." ✅

questions.text: "He ___ me that the project was competitive."
questions.hint: "told + person = He TOLD ME." "said" cannot have a person object! ✅

questions.text: "Where is the office?" → She asked where ___.
questions.hint: No inversion + backshift. "She asked where THE OFFICE WAS." ✅

questions.text: "Are you coming?" → He asked ___ I was coming.
questions.hint: yes/no → "whether" or "if". "He asked WHETHER I WAS COMING." ✅

questions.text: "Study harder!" → She told us ___.
questions.hint: "told + person + to + infinitive." "She told us TO STUDY harder." ✅

questions.text: "Don't be late!" → He told me ___ late.
questions.hint: "told + person + NOT TO + infinitive." "He told me NOT TO BE late." ✅

questions.text: "I've finished." → She said she ___ .
questions.hint: Backshift: Present Perfect → Past Perfect. "She said she HAD FINISHED." ✅

questions.text: "The discussion was animated." "Animated" means:
questions.hint: "animated" = lively, active, energetic.

questions.text: She ___ the lecture to check she had understood it correctly.
questions.hint: "paraphrase" = to express something in different words to show understanding.

questions.text: "Language was never static." "Static" means:
questions.hint: "static" = not changing; remaining the same.

questions.text: "The most endangered languages." "Endangered" means:
questions.hint: "endangered" = at risk of becoming extinct.

questions.text: "Speakers stopped transmitting the language." "Transmit" means:
questions.hint: "transmit" = to pass something (language, knowledge, culture) on to the next person or generation.
